ranked.headline: Modeling cell-state transitions from unpaired single-cell data with transport models
ranked.summary: U-Pert models unpaired single-cell perturbation data, while SupeRJump and DELPHAI infer fate and response via jump-diffusion or optimal transport formulations.

ranked.headline: Pretrained models are adapted to single-cell, spatial, and antibody prediction tasks
ranked.summary: Recent preprints reuse pretrained and self-supervised representations across single-cell, spatial, antibody, and pathology data.

ranked.headline: Sequence and structure descriptors drive peptide and disordered-protein design
ranked.summary: Metrics normalized against null models and free-energy landscapes are now used to generate designed peptides and polypeptides.

ranked.headline: Perturbation prediction r² is bounded by variance captured by the projection basis

ranked.headline: Structure-aware models now score, generate, and nominate ligands for protein targets
ranked.summary: Recent deep-learning and structure-based studies extend ligand binding prediction to macrocycles, generative design, and target nomination.

ranked.headline: Read-level models infer methylation, copy number and cancer signals from sequencing data

ranked.headline: Sequence-based models now interpret TF binding, nucleosome positioning and variant risk
ranked.summary: Base-pair and single-nucleotide resolution models are now paired with attribution and patient-level context to interpret regulatory and variant effects.

ranked.summary: Enhanced-sampling and path-sampling methods are now applied to Mg2+ binding, drug unbinding, and transporter transitions in recent preprints and publications.

ranked.summary: A sequence-only ΔTm model outperforms structure-informed methods, and new enzyme benchmarks target discovery-relevant specificity tasks.

ranked.headline: Genomic and molecular foundation models tested for transfer, protection, and scaling
ranked.summary: Foundation models for DNA, genomes, and molecules are now being evaluated on transfer, safeguarding, and downstream prediction tasks.

ranked.headline: Long-read and graph-based genomes resolve sex-biased expression and structural variation
ranked.summary: Long-read and pan-genome assemblies now resolve sex-biased expression, pathogenicity gene families, and structural variants across diverse taxa.

ranked.summary: Coarse-grained, all-atom and NEMD simulations now resolve assembly-level mechanisms spanning condensate interfaces and conformational selection.

ranked.headline: Read-level models refine splicing and expression estimates from RNA-seq
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply read-level and calibration models to correct splicing, normalization and k-mer quantification biases in RNA-seq.

ranked.headline: Spatial gene expression anchors cell states to tissue geometry and morphology
ranked.summary: Spatially resolved omics now supports generative, translational and statistical models linking gene expression to tissue position across scales.

ranked.headline: Deep learning and reprocessed datasets refine site-level prediction in proteomics

ranked.summary: Scaling causal discovery and network-informed statistics to multi-omics, multi-tissue, and rare-variant genetic data now yields candidate causal genes.

ranked.summary: Label-free optical imaging and coregistered mass spectrometry now feed physics-informed models that infer latent parameters without manual tuning.

ranked.headline: Transcriptome scans detect nonlinear lncRNA similarity and de novo inexact repeats
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend transcriptome analysis to nonlinear sequence similarity, de novo repeat discovery, and harmonized regulatory catalogs across tissues.

ranked.summary: Recent preprints model sensor-consumer fronts and test how cell aggregate geometry and receptor endocytosis reverse single-cell chemorepulsion.

ranked.summary: Chromosome-level HiFi and Hi-C assemblies now span Entamoeba, a keratitis-derived Fusarium isolate, and all 25 Aegilops species.
